title: Optimal Three-Part Differential–Linear Distinguishers
summary: Biases of three-part differential–linear distinguishers can be evaluated effectively, but jointly choosing their three components for optimal bias remains open.

formal_statement.body: In differential--linear cryptanalysis, consider distinguishers obtained by dividing a cipher into three parts and choosing a differential trail, a middle differential--linear pair, and a linear trail. Although the bias of a resulting distinguisher can be effectively evaluated, the unresolved task is to jointly select these three components so that the distinguisher's bias is optimal.

scope.domain: Differential–linear cryptanalysis of ciphers using three-part distinguishers.
parameters: Differential trail: component chosen for one part of the cipher
Middle differential–linear pair: component chosen for the middle part
Linear trail: component chosen for one part of the cipher
scope.unresolved_remainder: Jointly select the differential trail, middle differential–linear pair, and linear trail to obtain a distinguisher with optimal bias.

citations.label: Enhancing the DATF Technique in Differential-Linear Cryptanalysis

progress.summary: The source lists this question under “Open Problems and Future Works,” noting that biases can be evaluated effectively while finding an optimal distinguisher remains future research.
citation_labels: Cheng Che et al., Enhancing the DATF Technique in Differential-Linear Cryptanalysis
